q: Clifford+T circuits are universal for quantum computation. The T gate (π/8 phase gate) requires fault-tolerant implementation via 'magic state distillation'. The overhead of T gate implementation in a fault-tolerant architecture is approximately:
opts: O(1) physical qubits per T gate
O(log²(1/ε)) T gates to implement one T gate to accuracy ε (Solovay-Kitaev), or O(log(1/ε)) with optimal decomposition (Ross-Selinger)
exp: Solovay-Kitaev: any single-qubit gate can be approximated within ε using O(log^c(1/ε)) gates from a universal set (c ≈ 3.97). For T gates specifically, optimal decompositions (Ross-Selinger) achieve O(log(1/ε)) T gates. Magic state distillation adds space overhead to produce accurate T gate magic states.
